chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ṣafwān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about the shādhakūnah that is affected by semen from a wet dream: may one pray on it? He said: No.
So the proper understanding of this report is that it indicates a kind of recommendation, not prohibition.

key_terms.أَيُصَلِّي: whether one may perform salat on it
key_terms.الشَّاذَكُونَةِ: a type of carpet or spread upon which one may pray
key_terms.الِاحْتِلَامُ: nocturnal emission; here referring to semen affecting the item
key_terms.الْوَجْهُ: the correct juristic interpretation or reconciliation

ai.seo_question: Is it forbidden to pray on a shādhakūnah that has been touched by impurity from a wet dream?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of praying on a shādhakūnah when it has been affected by impurity from a wet dream. The apparent prohibition is understood here as indicating istihbab rather than strict forbiddance, showing a juristic distinction between disliked and prohibited matters in ritual purity and salat.
